Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Plant Plunged Into 16th Blackout of Year — The Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant was plunged into a complete blackout early Sunday morning, Nov. 8, after its final working 330 kV line, Ferrosplavna-1, disconnected from the Ukrainian grid, state operator Energoatom announced. The event marks the 16th external power blackout recorded at the station in 2026.

Russia Sends High-Level Delegation to Abu Dhabi Talks — Russia is sending a higher-level delegation to trilateral negotiations with Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11. Led by presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky, the team includes Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, GRU military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov, and General Staff officer Yuri Zhigarloffsky.

Zelensky Condemns Fatal Krakow Attack, Expresses Sympathy — President Volodymyr Zelensky offered condolences to the families of victims killed in the Krakow Market Square mass shooting on Saturday, Nov. 7, calling the incident a shocking crime and affirming Ukraine’s solidarity with Poland. The attack, carried out by a 24-year-old gunman armed with an AR-15 rifle, killed six people and injured 15 on the square before police found three bodies of presumed relatives at his residence.

Poland: Dispute over Constitutional Court Escalates — Commentators across Poland, France, Ireland, Latvia, Italy, and Romania have analyzed the escalating confrontation over Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal following the suspension of its leadership and nocturnal police operations. Polish outlets Gazeta Wyborcza and Rzeczpospolita have criticized the Tusk government’s heavy-handed tactics, while Polityka has condemned President Karol Nawrocki for physical obstruction.

Germany Exhausts Patriot Stockpiles for Ukraine, Pistorius Says — German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has announced that Berlin’s exhausted domestic stockpiles mean it can no longer supply additional Patriot air defense systems or missiles to Ukraine without creating unacceptable gaps in its own national security. Pistorius has urged other international allies to step up air defense transfers ahead of a Ramstein-format meeting in mid-November.

Russian Strike on Odesa Kills 1, Hits Infrastructure — A Russian strike on the southern port city of Odesa killed one person, damaged municipal infrastructure, and sparked a fire in a non-residential building on Saturday evening, Nov. 8, according to Odesa City Military Administration Head Serhii Lysak. Blast waves damaged windows in nearby residential properties.

Zelensky Mandates SBU Asset Declarations Amid Carthage Scandal — President Volodymyr Zelensky has announced a draft law restoring mandatory asset declarations for all SBU personnel following the “disgraceful” Operation Carthage scandal involving senior police and security officials. Zelensky confirmed initial dismissals within the SBU and stated that Ukraine is sharing intelligence with the US, Poland, and Germany regarding the transnational Khimprom synthetic narcotics syndicate.

Krakow Gunman Kills 9, Injures 15 — A 24-year-old gunman killed six people and injured 15 after opening fire on crowds in Krakow’s Main Market Square on Saturday, Nov. 7. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk classified the mass shooting as an act of terrorism, while President Karol Nawrocki declared national mourning for Nov. 8-9. Police arrested the masked suspect, who was armed with an AR-15 rifle, before discovering three bodies of presumed family members during subsequent searches at his reside

Ukraine War News Today - Top Stories and Breaking Updates from Kyiv Post — Stay informed with the most important Ukraine breaking news today. This page compiles the top headlines and critical updates from across Ukraine, offering a real-time snapshot of key developments. Whether it’s military updates, political changes, or international reactions — we bring you the latest Ukraine news as it happens. All reports are carefully curated from verified sources and KyivPost correspondents on the ground

Italian Pasta Giant Dodges Questions About Presence in Russia — In a Swedish town famous for its crispbread, the chairman of Italy’s Barilla pasta colossus recently received a prestigious honor. But amid the celebrations, one question went unanswered: Why is his company still doing business in Russia.

Kyiv Baroque Fest – 2026: Gesualdo, the Mozarts and the Hope of the Unknowable — Kyiv Baroque Fest returns for its third edition Nov. 12-22, bringing 32 events to the National Philharmonic of Ukraine. Concerts, lectures, masterclasses, discussions and a photography exhibition will explore the theme “Gesualdo / The Mozarts: Hope of the Unknowable.” The festival examines genius, ethics, gender roles and creative freedom while bringing together early music performers from seven countries.

IIHF Bars Belarus From 2027 Worlds, Weighs Russia Ruling — The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) has decided not to admit Belarusian men’s and under-20 teams to the 2027 World Championships, citing tournament organization and logistics. While the IIHF Disciplinary Board partially upheld a Belarusian appeal, it found no legal basis for immediate reinstatement.

Giorgia Meloni Has Wrong-Footed the Kremlin — Giorgia Meloni wants EU leaders to decide who can speak for them in Ukraine peace talks. Her letter to António Costa reflects a position she took before entering office: Ukraine’s right to defend its independence matters to Italy’s own security, even when defending it costs her votes.

Russian Drones Strike Kremenchuk Enterprises, Injuring 4 — A Russian strike drone attack hit private commercial enterprises across two separate locations in Kremenchuk, Poltava region, injuring four people and sparking structural fires on Saturday, Nov. 7. Regional Governor Vitalii Diakivnych confirmed the casualties and dispatch of emergency response services.

Russia Reroutes Pig Iron to Arctic Port Over Black Sea Strikes — Russian exporters have begun shipping pig iron through the Arctic port of Murmansk for the first time since 1996, rerouting cargoes away from the Black Sea following nearly 700 maritime strikes this year. The detour adds 10 days to voyage times to Mediterranean destinations like Turkey and increases freight costs by up to $100 per ton.

US Midterms: What Is the Global Impact? — Media commentators across Europe and the Middle East have analyzed the strategic implications of the Democratic Party’s victory in the US midterm elections: what is known about the potential constraints on Donald Trump’s executive authority, the impact on the armed conflict with Iran, military assistance for Ukraine, and technology regulation.

Zelensky Says Russia Used North Korean KN-23 Missiles on Grid — President Volodymyr Zelensky has announced that Russian forces used North Korean KN-23 ballistic missiles in an overnight strike on a key Ukrainian energy facility, with air defenses able to intercept only four of 36 ballistic missiles due to an acute shortage of Patriot interceptors. The president urged Washington to expedite missile deliveries ahead of the winter season and trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi.

Europe Hit by Wave of Bomb Hoaxes Targeting Media, Flights — Coordinated bomb threats have targeted European media newsrooms and dozens of commercial passenger flights, triggering office evacuations in Dublin, flight diversions in Prague, and NATO fighter jet scrambles. Broadcasters in Ireland, Bulgaria, and Britain received threatening emails sent under the pseudonym “Mikhail Andropov,” while previous threats earlier in the week invoked a banned Russian extremist group.

Budanov to Pay Fine After Language Violation in Kyiv Suburb — State Language Protection Commissioner Olena Ivanovska has announced that Head of the Presidential Office Kyrylo Budanov acknowledged violating Ukraine’s state language legislation and will pay the mandatory statutory fine. The violation occurred when Budanov used Russian while addressing a crowd during violent clashes outside a National Guard transit house in Petropavlivska Borshchahivka on Nov. 2.
Another Major Corruption Scandal Shakes Ukraine — A leading Ukrainian anti-corruption activist shares her response to what has just been uncovered.

Nobody Knows Anything — The 2026 US election reshaped Congress but provided few clear answers about what comes next for Ukraine. While Democrats gained control of both chambers, foreign policy remains largely in the hands of the White House, and it is unclear whether the new majority will prioritize Ukraine-related legislation or focus on oversight and domestic issues.

Russia Strikes Central Ukraine Naftogaz Facility 3 Times — Russian forces carried out three consecutive strikes against a Naftogaz oil and gas facility in central Ukraine overnight into Saturday, Nov. 7, damaging equipment and triggering a major fire. Acting Board Chairman Serhiy Fedorenko confirmed that early evacuations prevented worker casualties.

Trump Touts ‘Grand Deal’ as Europe, Kyiv Voice Alarm — US President Donald Trump has claimed that Russia and Ukraine “for the first time want to make a deal,” touting an expansive European settlement framework ahead of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11. However, European diplomats and President Volodymyr Zelensky have voiced concern over the lack of concrete details surrounding the proposal outlined by Jared Kushner.

Trump: You’re Fired — Post-election diplomacy will be interesting. Given the size of their victory, the Democrats could and should pass legislation to provide Patriot missiles to Ukraine immediately, as well as to push Trump to impose the sledgehammer bill of sanctions on Russia formulated by the late Senator Lindsey Graham.

Norway Allocates 500M Kroner for Ukrainian Civil Services — The Norwegian government has announced an allocation of 500 million Norwegian kroner ($54 million) through the World Bank to finance Ukraine’s state budget for early 2027. The funding will cover salaries for teachers and healthcare workers, state pensions, and social payments. Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide has emphasized that maintaining public institutions is essential to national resilience.

Russia Cracks Down on Those Questioning pro-Putin Poll Results — Political scientist Alexander Kynev and environmental activist Dmitry Morozov were arrested on drug charges in Russia after publicly alleging fraud in the September parliamentary elections. Relatives and defense lawyers stated that security services beat both men, subjecting Morozov to electric shocks and inflicting a double leg fracture on Kynev.

Ukraine Hits 2 Iskander Launchers, Pantsir in Bryansk — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine has announced that precision strikes on Nov. 6 and overnight into Nov. 7 hit two Iskander operational-tactical missile launchers and a Pantsir-S1 air defense system in Russia’s Bryansk region. Ukrainian forces also struck rear logistics warehouses in the occupied Luhansk region and a drone operator staging area in the Zaporizhzhia region.

Russia Fires 36 Ballistics at Kyiv and Region Overnight in Major Barrage — Russian forces fired 36 ballistic missiles and 172 strike drones overnight into Saturday, Nov. 7, aiming all 36 ballistic missiles directly at Kyiv and the surrounding metropolitan region. President Volodymyr Zelensky said the barrage was intended to force power blackouts ahead of planned trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi. The strikes wounded nine people, including a child, hit the North Bridge and a kindergarten, and damaged

Russian Glide Bombs Strike Sumy, Injuring 7 — Russian tactical aircraft launched six guided aerial bombs (KABs) against Sumy on Friday, Nov. 6, wounding seven people across four sites in the Zarichnyi and Kovpakivskyi districts. Four victims were hospitalized, and more than 15 residential buildings sustained damage alongside gas and power disruptions.

EBRD Seeks €500M to Repair Chornobyl Drone Damage — The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is seeking at least €500 million ($545 million) to repair the New Safe Confinement at the Chornobyl nuclear power plant after a Russian drone strike punctured its protective arch. G7 nations have pledged €260 million ($283 million), with France, Ukraine, and the EBRD set to co-chair a donor conference in Paris on Nov. 9. Officials warned repairs must conclude by 2030 to prevent corrosi

Trump Promises “Major Deal” On Ukraine | Bohdan Nahaylo — US President Donald Trump claims that a breakthrough agreement with Russia may be within reach, one that could not only bring an end to the war in Ukraine but also reshape Europe’s security architecture. On World Talks, Bohdan Nahaylo, Editor-in-Chief of the Kyiv Post, argues that following the US midterm elections, Trump is trying to regain and preserve his image as an effective dealmaker. At the same time, NATO’s Secretary General has s

Komyshuvakha Death Toll Hits 55 as HUR Names Russian Pilots — The death toll from a Russian airstrike on an aid distribution point and shelter in Komyshuvakha has risen to 55 after rescuers recovered nine more bodies from the rubble. Ukraine’s military intelligence (HUR) has identified the Russian colonel who planned the strike and six Su-34 pilots who dropped the guided bombs, including a 3,000-kilogram FAB-3000 munition. Intelligence analysts estimate that roughly 30 more bodies may remain tra

Drones Strike Saratov Refinery, Missiles Hit Oryol Plant — Ukrainian strike drones attacked the Saratov Oil Refinery while precision missiles struck the Proton defense microelectronics plant in Oryol overnight into Saturday, Nov. 7. The strikes triggered major fires across both strategic installations, damaging a Rosneft refinery with an annual capacity of 7 million metric tons and an enterprise supplying semiconductors for Iskander-M missiles and Pantsir-S1 systems.

Zelensky, Drapatyi Prepare Military Command Reshuffle — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Friday, Nov. 6, that he and Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) Commander-in-Chief Mykhailo Drapatyi are preparing personnel reshuffles within the military leadership as Kyiv prepares for upcoming diplomatic tracks. Zelensky also held consultations with the Nordic-Baltic Eight (NB8) group to secure urgent winter assistance, while confirming ongoing coordination for tripartite formats involving the US, Eur

Budanov: Russia Strikes Energy Grid to Spark Protests — Head of the Presidential Office Kyrylo Budanov has said that Russia is targeting Ukraine’s critical infrastructure to cause severe damage, hoping to trigger social discontent, street protests, and concessions on national interests. Budanov asserted the plan will fail, affirming Ukraine will endure the winter. The warning came as President Volodymyr Zelensky said intelligence indicates Russia is preparing renewed strikes on civilian utilitie

Poland Pledges €1.8M Zlotys for Generators, Eyes Abu Dhabi Talks — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski announced on Friday, Nov. 6, that Warsaw will provide an additional 8 million zlotys ($2 million) to purchase power generators for Ukraine ahead of winter. Speaking after a Council of the Baltic Sea States meeting in Warsaw attended by Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha and EU High Representative Kaja Kallas, Sikorski warned that no diplomatic solution can be imposed on Kyiv without

Russian Drone Hits Kyiv Region Home, Killing 1 — A Russian strike drone hit a private home in the village of Bohdanivka in Kyiv region’s Brovary district on Friday evening, Nov. 6, destroying the building, causing a fire, and killing one man. The strike coincided with an overnight Russian barrage of at least six ballistic missiles targeting Kyiv overnight. The capital attack injured five people, including a child, and destroyed a building on kindergarten grounds in the Solomianskyi district.

Why Russia Wants Into the Turkic States Organization – and Why That Could Break It — Kazakhstan’s proposal to involve Russia in the Organization of Turkic States has sparked Crimean Tatar opposition and concerns over Moscow’s ambitions. As Turkey expands military cooperation and alternative trade routes across Central Asia, Russia’s potential admission raises questions about the bloc’s independence and future.

‘We Will Not Implement It’: Kallas Rejects US-Russia Security Deal Negotiated Without Europe — EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas warned that Europe would refuse to implement any US-Russia security agreement negotiated without its participation. She rejected territorial concessions, demanded Russian accountability and warned against allowing Moscow to rearm under a peace deal.

‘Ceasefire First’: Poland Warns Against US-Russia Deal on Europe’s Security — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski rejected any security agreement negotiated without Ukraine and Europe, insisting on a ceasefire before talks with Moscow. He also demanded tougher sanctions, restrictions on Russian tourist visas and greater support for Ukraine.

‘We Don’t Want Yalta 2.0’: Zelensky Warns Trump’s Russia-Europe Security Deal Could Be ‘Dangerous’ — President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Washington’s proposed Europe-Russia security framework risks dividing the continent, insisting that ending the war and securing Ukraine must come first.

Russian Ballistic Missiles Strike Kyiv, Destroy Kindergarten Building, Injure Child, 4 Others — Russia launched at least six ballistic missiles toward Kyiv overnight Nov. 6-7, injuring five people, including a child. A kindergarten building was destroyed, several apartment buildings were damaged, and fires broke out in the capital.

Ukraine Approves Unified Procedure for Identifying Deceased Military Personnel, Civilians — Ukraine’s government, led by Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi, has approved a single, unified procedure for the regional interagency teams that identify the bodies of fallen soldiers and civilians and prevent losses of identification data. The new rules standardize inspections, forensic examinations, biological sampling and documentation. According to Koretskyi on Friday, Nov. 6, the 2027 budget includes m

Trump Names Migration Hardliner Miller New Chief of Staff — US President Donald Trump named Stephen Miller, his deputy chief of staff and the architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new White House chief of staff on Friday, Nov. 6. Miller, 41, will replace Susie Wiles, the first woman to hold the post, starting Monday, Nov. 9, while Wiles moves to Trump’s political operation. The appointment comes after Republicans lost control of both the House and Senate to Democrats in the midter

Zelensky Warns of Fresh Russian Strikes on Bridges, Energy Grid — President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Friday, Nov. 6, that Ukrainian intelligence shows Russia is preparing a new attack on the country’s civilian and energy infrastructure, and bridges across the Dnipro River. He urged Ukraine’s partners not to delay deliveries of Patriot interceptors and called on Ukrainian residents to heed air raid alerts, amid the threat of missile strikes. Ukraine, he said, would continue its strikes on Russi

UK Apologizes to Ukrainian Pupils as New Language GCSE Announced — UK government ministers have announced a new Ukrainian General Certificate of Secondary Education (GCSE) for England, Wales and Northern Ireland, with teaching expected from September 2028 and first assessments in 2029. Schools Minister Georgia Gould apologized to refugees encouraged to take Russian in its absence, whilst Education Secretary Lucy Powell said Ukrainian pupils should have every opportunity to preserve the connectio

Russian Strike in Zhytomyr Strains Kyiv’s Power, Water Supply, Klitschko Says — A Russian attack on an energy facility in Zhytomyr, western Ukraine, has reportedly worsened power supply to Kyiv and reduced water pressure in the capital, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Friday, Nov. 6. Kyivvodokanal is switching power to generators at its stations where possible, while repair crews assess the damage in Zhytomyr, according to Zhytomyr Regional Military Administration head Vitali Bunechko. The disrup

‘No Decisions on Europe Without Europe’: Sybiha, Kallas Press Russia Ahead of Abu Dhabi — Speaking alongside EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and Poland’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Radoslaw Sikorski on Friday, Nov. 6. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said that Europe must be a part of the peace process both before and after the next meeting in Abu Dhabi. Sybiha also listed Kyiv’s priorities, naming security guarantees, an energy truce and the return of abducted Ukra

Prosecutors Seek $2.2M Bail for SBU General in NABU Case — Prosecutors have requested detention with Hr. 100 million ($2.2 million) bail for SBU general Serhiy Duka in the Operation Carthage investigation. Separately, bail has been paid for senior police official Volodymyr Tsenov, while NABU confirmed searching Kyiv regional police chief Andriy Rubel’s home without serving him with a formal notice of suspicion.

Kyiv Commits Additional $22M to Defense Forces, Supplies 2,700 Drones to Assault Brigade — Kyiv has delivered nearly 2,700 drones and 12 ground robotic systems (GRCs) to the 5th Separate Assault Brigade, the capital’s Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Friday, Nov. 6. The shipment, he said, includes 2,200 first-person-view (FPV) drones and 450 reconnaissance drones. On Thursday, Nov. 5, the Kyiv City Council allocated an extra Hr. 1 billion ($22 million) for Ukraine’s Security and Defense Forces, bring

Damaged Grid Forces Ukraine to Export Power as Kyiv Faces Blackouts, Expert Says — Russian strikes have left Ukraine exporting some electricity even as residents of its capital face prolonged outages, according to an energy analyst. Repeated attacks have interrupted repairs to the substations Kyiv relies on for power.

‘The Worst Situation’: Zelensky and Klitschko Clash Over Energy Crisis — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv faces Ukraine’s worst utility disruptions following Russian strikes, blaming shortcomings in municipal preparations. Mayor Vitali Klitschko defended the city’s efforts, saying approval of its resilience plan had been delayed for nearly six months, warning that infrastructure cannot withstand repeated attacks without stronger air defenses. In a follow-up statement, Klitschko accused the

Trump Jr. Discusses Deals With Russian Oligarch, Report Says — Donald Trump Jr. discussed business deals in Kazakhstan with Kremlin-linked businessman Umar Kremlev, according to two sources cited by IStories. The specific proposals remain unknown. Trump Jr.’s spokesperson said the two are personal friends who have never entered into business deals together and have no plans to do so.

Nate Vance: ‘One Thing You Can’t Buy Is Courage’ — The US vice president’s cousin, Nate Vance, has been fighting for the Ukrainian cause on the battlefield and in the rear since the early days of the full-scale invasion. Lord Ashcroft asks him what Americans back home should be aware of when it comes to Ukraine.

Russia Used Oleshky Truce to Reinforce Front — Russia moved more than 1,000 troops into occupied Kherson region during a temporary ceasefire around Oleshky, Ukraine's 34th Marine Brigade said. Ukrainian forces warn Moscow may be preparing an advance toward Kherson but report no large-scale assaults so far.

UADamage Secures US Funding to Scale AI Tech — Ukrainian startup UADamage secured investments from US based Pravo Ventures and Ondas Capital to accelerate its AI powered demining technologies. The capital will support the integration of multi-sensor data and the global rollout of these solutions for defense and humanitarian operators.

Japan Demands Russia Return Control of Four Japan Tobacco Businesses — Tokyo has formally protested Russia’s decision to put four Japan Tobacco businesses under the control of a Russian company. The order affects the country’s largest tobacco producer and follows similar moves against Nestlé and Auchan.

Kyiv Warns Heating Utility Raids Threaten Energy Projects — Investigators searched offices and homes of Kyivteploenergo employees, Kyiv authorities said, warning that the possible seizure of original documents could disrupt energy resilience projects. The utility says the design work remains unpaid and completion certificates have not been signed. City officials suggested the searches could represent political pressure as Russian attacks strain the capital’s heating and power systems.

UK, France to Lead First Major Drill for Post-Ceasefire Ukraine Force — Exercise Koalicja will test whether troops from 11 countries can move equipment across borders, operate under one command and keep a multinational force supplied. Britain and France have declared their intent to deploy after a ceasefire. Poland has ruled out sending its own troops into Ukraine.

Russia Proposes Letting Airlines Keep Foreign-Leased Jets Through 2028 — Russia’s Transport Ministry has drafted a two-year extension to wartime rules that allowed airlines to retain aircraft after foreign leasing companies demanded their return. Russian carriers still depend on Western-built jets as domestic manufacturers work to deliver replacements.

Ukraine Seeks New Contract for Starshield Amid Connectivity Challenges — Despite the still unexplained speed limitations imposed on Ukraine by the Starshield satellite network last month, Kyiv is pushing for renewal of the agreement with the US government due to expire in mid-2027.

My 5 Years as Kyiv Post CEO: The People Behind Ukraine’s Global Voice — This Nov. 11, I will be marking my fifth anniversary as CEO, but I feel it would be only right to honor our incredible team who rebuilt Kyiv Post through war – and our shared commitment to keeping Ukraine's voice heard around the world.

Bomb Threats Hit Dozens of European Airports — At least 30 flights were hit by bomb hoaxes across Europe on Thursday after similar incidents on Tuesday affected seven flights and a cruise ship. While the perpetrator remains unclear, experts suggest they fit the modus operandi of state actors, as Europe warns of heightened hybrid threats from adversaries. One email was reportedly signed off by an anti-feminist group in Russia, but its founder denied any involvement.

Ukraine Plans to Resume Medical Evacuation Flights by Year-End — Ukraine has approved rules for State Emergency Service aircraft to transfer patients between hospitals and take them abroad for specialist care. Crews will also be able to carry transplant teams and donor organs when the journey by road would take too long.

Costa Backs Meloni’s Call to Settle Who Speaks for EU at Ukraine Peace Talks — European Council President António Costa has agreed to discuss who should represent the EU in negotiations on Russia’s war against Ukraine. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wants leaders to settle the question in December, warning that Rome could be asked to honor commitments it never approved.

Russian Bombing of Komyshuvakha Kills 53, Search Continues — The death toll from Russia's Nov. 2 airstrike on Komyshuvakha in Zaporizhzhia region has risen to 53. Rescuers continue searching the rubble, while Zelensky says dozens were still missing as of Thursday.

NATO Chief Sees Ukraine War Ending in ‘Compromise’ — NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said an outright victory for either side was unlikely. He warned that the end of fighting would free up Russian troops now deployed in Ukraine and stressed the US role in Europe’s defense.

EU Sends Ukraine $4.9 Billion for Budget and Defense — The European Commission paid Ukraine €3.7 billion in budget support and €658 million for defense procurement on Nov. 5. A further €25.2 billion in EU financing remains available this year if Kyiv meets the conditions for release.

Zelensky: Ukraine Has Not Received $16 Billion in Previously Agreed US Aid — Ukraine has not received $16 billion in previously agreed US assistance, Zelensky said. He called for continued efforts to secure the outstanding funds and negotiate new American defense support.
British Defence Intelligence Update Ukraine 5 November , 2026 — Latest from the British Defence Intelligence.

US Midterms Offer Hope on Ukraine Aid, Russia Scrutiny: Analysts — Democrats’ victory in the US midterm elections could help restore military and economic aid to Ukraine and increase scrutiny of Trump’s Russia policy. Analysts say the new Congress may limit further US disengagement, though Trump’s foreign policy powers remain substantial.

Russia’s War in Ukraine Fuels Prosthetics Boom With Links to Putin’s Inner Circle — Russia’s prosthetics industry has expanded sharply since the 2022 invasion, generating nearly €202 million in revenue in 2025. An investigation found that companies linked to Putin’s inner circle and regional officials are benefiting from rising demand and public spending.

Russia’s Major Oil Refinery Reportedly Targeted as 142 Drones Downed — The Afipsky Oil Refinery in Russia’s Krasnodar Krai was reportedly targeted by drones on Friday, with explosions and smoke reported nearby. Russia said it downed 142 Ukrainian UAVs overnight, but Kyiv Post could not independently verify the refinery attack.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 5, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 5, 2026.

Meloni Urges Single EU Voice in Ukraine Talks, Warns of ‘Irrelevance’ — Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni criticized Europe’s fragmented approach to Ukraine peace negotiations, warning that overlapping diplomatic initiatives undermine the bloc’s credibility. She called for a single EU representative with a clear negotiating mandate, while European Council President António Costa agreed to raise the issue with EU leaders.

Canada Plans $1.8 Billion Drone Investment, Ukraine to Receive Production Share — Canada plans to spend at least C$2.3 billion ($1.8 billion) over five years on military drones and counter-drone systems under its proposed 2026 federal budget. The investment follows an agreement with Ukraine to expand joint drone production, with Ottawa pledging to send one-third of Canadian-made drones to Kyiv.

Kushner Unveils 5-Point European Security Plan Ahead of Peace Talks — US presidential adviser Jared Kushner outlined five objectives for a new European security framework ahead of trilateral peace negotiations with Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi next week. The proposal emphasizes crisis communications, military transparency, de-escalation, and national sovereignty, while preserving NATO’s central role in European defense.

Ukraine to Hold Elections if US Brokers Winter Ceasefire With Russia — President Volodymyr Zelensky revealed that he asked Washington to negotiate a winter ceasefire with Russia that could protect Ukraine’s energy supplies and create conditions for presidential elections. In a German television interview, he said voting under martial law would be unfair to soldiers on the front lines, refugees abroad, and residents of Russian-occupied territories.

Melania Trump Receives Ukraine’s Order of Princess Olga — US First Lady Melania Trump received Ukraine’s Order of Princess Olga, First Class, during a White House ceremony celebrating the Oleshky humanitarian ceasefire. Ukrainian officials urged her to expand the initiative, while Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev credited Putin with supporting the operation. The First Lady also announced that she had written personal letters to both presidents, though their contents were not disclosed.

Trump Met Putin’s Envoy at White House, Skipped Ukrainian Delegation — US President Donald Trump confirmed on Thursday that he met Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House but did not meet Ukrainian officials who were also visiting for a humanitarian ceremony hosted by First Lady Melania Trump. Trump claimed a settlement to Russia’s war against Ukraine was close and suggested a broader agreement could involve all of Europe.

Sybiha Expects ‘New Dynamic’ in US Support for Ukraine After Midterms — Kyiv expects a shift in US support for Ukraine following the conclusion of midterm elections, in which Republicans suffered sweeping losses. Speaking during a conference in Bucharest on Thursday, Nov. 5, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said Ukraine’s security is inseparable from that of the US, while claiming that Russia is showing no real sign of serious interest in negotiations.
